status_definitions.rejected_removed: The current compiler deliberately rejects a removed spelling and emits a directed migration diagnostic.
status_definitions.rejected_syntax: The current compiler rejects this language shape as invalid syntax; the diagnostic is still a compiler result rather than an LSP failure.
status_definitions.accepted: The current compiler parser and semantic sources contain the construct, or its direct compiler behavior is covered by the referenced compiler tests.
status_definitions.diagnostic_passthrough: The LSP must preserve the compiler diagnostic and recovery behavior; it must not claim that a provider supports the construct.
status_definitions.unsupported: The compiler accepts the construct, but the named LSP providers deliberately return their documented no-match shape until they have exact semantic identity or workspace data.
status_definitions.partial: The LSP covers only the providers and cases named by the entry; other providers must not infer support from that partial coverage.

regression_buckets.compiler_regression: A changed or missing compiler probe, parser source reference, or compiler source fingerprint is triaged as frontend/toolchain drift before changing LSP behavior.
regression_buckets.server_regression: A provider test failing while the compiler provenance and probe results are unchanged is triaged as an LSP regression.
regression_buckets.inventory_staleness: A newer pinned compiler source or backend binary requires re-running this inventory and recording the new provenance before any support claim changes.

lsp_provider_limits.construct: Imported modules, qualified module members, and cross-file references
lsp_provider_limits.behavior: Providers use only exact same-document retained resolver edges; qualified, imported, or cross-file targets return null or [] according to the provider contract.

lsp_provider_limits.construct: Overloaded functions with more than one declaration sharing a name
lsp_provider_limits.behavior: Navigation and signature help decline ambiguous names instead of guessing an overload; the compiler remains the authority for call resolution and diagnostics.

lsp_provider_limits.construct: A local or parameter shadowing a top-level declaration
lsp_provider_limits.behavior: Definition declines local binding targets because the compiler has no local declaration edge. Signature help declines a call when a local or parameter shadows the top-level callable; it does not fabricate a name-only target. References and documentHighlight support parameter/local BindingIds with exact spans.

lsp_provider_limits.construct: Struct fields, enum variants, constructors, and method/member calls
lsp_provider_limits.behavior: The current providers do not expose member or variant identity as navigation/signature targets; they return their documented no-match result while semantic tokens and diagnostics may still represent the source.

lsp_provider_limits.construct: Named, generic-specialized, variadic, dynamic, synthetic effect-handler, and constructor calls
lsp_provider_limits.behavior: Signature help is limited to one positional call edge targeting a unique non-constructor top-level function; all other call forms return null.
